Refusals, NA, NULL and Zero

Source: vignettes/refusals-and-na.Rmd
refusals-and-na.Rmd

The most damaging error a creel estimate can carry is not a crash. It is a believable number that quietly treats something unknown as zero: a stratum nobody sampled counted as no effort, a standard error that was never propagated shown as 0. This page explains the rules tidycreel follows to keep those apart, and why it sometimes refuses to give an answer at all.

Three rules:

zero      a measurement: none was seen. It counts.
NA        unknown: a value exists but was not measured. It is never read as zero.
refusal   the data cannot support the estimate asked for. No number is returned.
library(tidycreel)

Zero is a measurement

A party that fished and caught nothing has a catch of 0, and that 0 belongs in every rate. Dropping zero-catch trips would make the rate an average over successful trips only, and too high. So tidycreel keeps them, and says how many there are, in case a missing value was recorded as 0:

design <- creel_design(example_season_calendar, date = date, strata = day_type)
design <- add_counts(design, example_season_counts,
  period_length_col = daylight_hours
)
design <- add_interviews(design, example_season_interviews,
  catch = catch_total, harvest = catch_kept, effort = hours_fished,
  trip_status = trip_status, n_anglers = n_anglers
)
#> ℹ 153 interviews have zero catch.
#>   Zero catch is usual; check it is not missing data recorded as 0.
#> ℹ Added 231 interviews: 172 complete (74%), 59 incomplete (26%)

The message is a prompt to check the data, not a sign that anything was changed. A count of 0 anglers is also an observation, but of one moment: no one was fishing when the count was made. It belongs in the estimate as a 0, like any other count. On its own it does not say that nobody fished that day; the expansion from counts to effort is what accounts for the rest of the day.

Unknown is not zero

A value that was never measured is a different thing, and the danger is that arithmetic treats it as zero without saying so. Leaving a stratum out of a sum is the same as adding 0 for it. tidycreel refuses at the points where that would happen.

A stratum with no sampled days

Here the weekend counts are removed, so no weekend day was counted:

weekday_counts <- example_season_counts[
  example_season_counts$day_type == "weekday",
]
weekday_only <- creel_design(example_season_calendar,
  date = date, strata = day_type
)
weekday_only <- add_counts(weekday_only, weekday_counts,
  period_length_col = daylight_hours
)

estimate_effort(weekday_only, target = "period_total")
#> Error in `refuse_unsampled_cells()`:
#> ! Expanded effort cannot be estimated: 1 calendar cell has no sampled
#>   day.
#> • day_type=weekend (34 days)
#> ✖ The days in an unsampled stratum would be left out of the total, reporting
#>   their unknown effort as zero.
#> ℹ Sample at least one day in every stratum, or merge the stratum into another
#>   before estimating.

A season total needs the weekend’s effort, and there is no information about it. Summing the weekday strata alone would report the 34 weekend days as zero effort. The default target asks a smaller question, the effort on the days that were counted, and that one has an answer:

estimate_effort(weekday_only)
#> 
#> ── Creel Survey Estimates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Method: Total
#> Variance: Taylor linearization
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> Effort target: sampled_days
#> Unit: angler-hours
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   estimate    se se_between se_within ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>      <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1     2576  346.       346.         0    1866.    3286.    28

A stratum with no catch rate

A total multiplies each stratum’s effort by its rate. If one stratum has effort but no interviews, its catch is unknown:

weekday_interviews <- example_season_interviews[
  example_season_interviews$day_type == "weekday",
]
no_weekend_rate <- creel_design(example_season_calendar,
  date = date, strata = day_type
)
no_weekend_rate <- add_counts(no_weekend_rate, example_season_counts,
  period_length_col = daylight_hours
)
no_weekend_rate <- add_interviews(no_weekend_rate, weekday_interviews,
  catch = catch_total, harvest = catch_kept, effort = hours_fished,
  trip_status = trip_status, n_anglers = n_anglers
)
#> ℹ 128 interviews have zero catch.
#>   Zero catch is usual; check it is not missing data recorded as 0.
#> ℹ Added 190 interviews: 138 complete (73%), 52 incomplete (27%)

estimate_total_catch(no_weekend_rate)
#> Error in `check_missing_rate_strata()`:
#> ! 1 effort cell has no rate in "estimate_total_catch".
#> ✖ No usable interviews for: day_type = weekend.
#> ✖ Their contribution to the total is unknown, not zero: 490 effort units, 16%
#>   of the effort being totalled.
#> ℹ Collect or attach interviews for that cell, or group more coarsely so it
#>   shares a rate.
#> ℹ `missing_rate = "exclude"` reports the total over the covered cells only, and
#>   records what it left out.

The refusal says how much effort has no rate, so you can judge whether it matters. If a total over the covered strata is what you want, ask for it. The result says what it left out, and keeps a record of it:

weekday_total <- estimate_total_catch(no_weekend_rate,
  missing_rate = "exclude"
)
#> Warning: 1 effort cell with no rate excluded from "estimate_total_catch".
#> ! Excluded: day_type = weekend (490 effort units, 16%).
#> ℹ The total covers the remaining cells only; see excluded_strata on the result.
weekday_total
#> 
#> ── Creel Survey Estimates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Method: Total Catch (Effort × CPUE)
#> Variance: Taylor linearization
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> Effort target: sampled_days
#> Unit: fish
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   estimate    se ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>      <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1     536.  136.     267.     806.   138
#> 
#> Covers the cells with a rate only. Excluded (no rate), see $excluded_strata:
#>   day_type = weekend: 490 effort units
weekday_total$excluded_strata
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   day_type effort_excluded excluded_from       
#>   <chr>              <dbl> <chr>               
#> 1 weekend              490 estimate_total_catch

The warning is the point: this total is the weekday catch, not the season’s, and nothing about the number says so except the warning and the record.

Other unknowns that are refused

  • A missing catch count. add_catch() refuses a species row whose count is NA. Dropping the row is not neutral: a missing "harvested" row means 0 harvested, and a missing "caught" row changes how total catch is derived. You decide whether to fill the value or drop the row.
  • An ambiguous column. Given two numeric columns and no count_col, add_counts() refuses rather than pick one, because expanding the wrong column into effort would give a confident wrong answer.
  • Units that cannot be told apart. These are not refused: the estimate is returned with an unknown unit, NA. vignette("unit-rules") explains why.

NULL, NA and zero in a standard error

The standard error of an aerial effort estimate has parts: the variation between sampled days, and the uncertainty in each correction applied to the counts. Each part is recorded in se_components, and each can be in one of three states:

State Meaning Effect on se
absent not propagated: it does not apply, or no standard error was supplied se leaves it out
NA applies, and is unknown se is NA
0 known to be exactly zero included, as zero

One exception to “absent”: a bootstrap se can contain a part it cannot report separately. On the bootstrap path of estimate_effort_aerial_glmm() the visibility and angler-ratio parts are inside se but not listed.

The three are kept apart because a zero is otherwise indistinguishable from a part nobody propagated. The aerial visibility correction shows all three:

aerial_calendar <- unique(data.frame(
  date = example_aerial_counts$date,
  day_type = example_aerial_counts$day_type
))

aerial_effort <- function(...) {
  design <- creel_design(aerial_calendar,
    date = date, strata = day_type,
    survey_type = "aerial", h_open = 14, angler_ratio = 1,
    angler_ratio_se = 0, ...
  )
  estimate_effort(add_counts(design, example_aerial_counts))
}

A correction was measured, but its standard error was not supplied. The visibility part is absent, and the standard error covers the count sampling only:

aerial_effort(visibility_correction = 0.85)
#> 
#> ── Creel Survey Estimates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Method: aerial_total
#> Variance: Taylor linearization
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> Effort target: sampled_days
#> Unit: angler-hours
#> Count-sampling SE: 774.4 (included in se)
#> within_day: 0 (included in se)
#> angler_ratio: 0 (included in se)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   estimate    se se_between se_within ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>      <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1   10492.  774.       774.         0    8831.   12153.    16

The correction’s standard error is supplied, so it is propagated:

aerial_effort(visibility_correction = 0.85, visibility_se = 0.04)
#> 
#> ── Creel Survey Estimates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Method: aerial_total
#> Variance: Taylor linearization
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> Effort target: sampled_days
#> Unit: angler-hours
#> Count-sampling SE: 774.4 (included in se)
#> within_day: 0 (included in se)
#> visibility: 493.7 (included in se)
#> angler_ratio: 0 (included in se)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   estimate    se se_between se_within ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>      <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1   10492.  918.       774.         0    8522.   12462.    16

No correction was studied ("none"). The point estimate divides by 1, but how many anglers the observer missed is unknown, so the standard error is too:

aerial_effort(visibility_correction = "none")
#> 
#> ── Creel Survey Estimates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Method: aerial_total
#> Variance: Taylor linearization
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> Effort target: sampled_days
#> Unit: angler-hours
#> Count-sampling SE: 658.3 (known, but se is `NA`)
#> within_day: 0 (known, but se is `NA`)
#> visibility: NA (unknown, so se is `NA`)
#> angler_ratio: 0 (known, but se is `NA`)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   estimate    se se_between se_within ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>      <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1     8918    NA       658.         0       NA       NA    16

The same counts give a standard error of 774, then 918, then NA. In the first, the visibility correction is a measured number whose uncertainty was not supplied, so 774 understates the total uncertainty by whatever that part would add (918 once it is supplied). In the third there is no measurement at all, and no honest standard error. In all three, angler_ratio: 0 is the third state: angler_ratio_se = 0 states that every person counted is an angler, exactly. A correction known exactly must be said to be: visibility_correction = 1, visibility_se = 0, for example, where every angler can be seen.

One exception: se_within with one count per day

With one count per day, estimate_effort() reports se_within = 0. It is not a measured zero: with a single count the variation within a day cannot be separated from the variation between days, and both are in se_between. So se is right, and only the split is not identified. vignette("effort-pipeline") explains this, and reporting it as NA instead is proposed for the next major release (issue #504).

Kinds of refusal

What is wrong Example What to do
a stratum or cell has no data no sampled day in a stratum; effort with no rate; one sampled day in a stratum, so no variance sample it, merge strata, or ask a narrower question
the input is ambiguous two candidate count columns; repeated rows for one sampling unit name the column; give the count time, or fix the rows
a required value is unknown an NA catch count; an aerial design without h_open or angler_ratio supply it, or state "none" where that is allowed
the estimator does not apply estimate_effort() on a camera design; a mean-of-ratios total on a bus route use the function the message names

A rate and an effort in different units are not on this list. A rate per party-hour times effort in angler-hours returns a total with a warning and unit NA, because the number may still be what you want if every party is one angler; vignette("unit-rules") shows it.

A refusal says what was wrong and, where there is a remedy, what to do. Many also carry a condition class beginning creel_error_ (creel_error_unsampled_cell, creel_error_missing_rate_strata, creel_error_single_psu, …), so that code can catch a particular refusal by name. Warnings, which return an estimate but say something about it, are listed in ?creel_warnings.

Why refuse rather than warn

A warning still returns a number, and a number travels: into a table, a report, a management decision, long after the warning has scrolled away. When the data cannot support the estimate, tidycreel does not return one. When they can support a narrower one, the refusal says how to ask for it, and that estimate is labelled as narrower.
